sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1990/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024

undefined original claimant, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 17.12.2011 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Dahod in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.2693 of 2004 (Old MACP no.805 of 1999), by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.65,000 /- with 9% per annum interest from the date of filing claim petition till its realization, to the claimant, holding Opponents No.1 and 2 i.e. driver and owner of the vehicle in question, liable,
jointly and several.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.2693 of 2004
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It is noted that the claim petition is dismissed against opponent No.3 - insurance company.

2. Brief facts of the case, as per claimant/s, are as under :
2.1

That on 23.01.1999 at about 10:00 a.m., the appellant - original claimant has been residing at village Bhitodi, Tal. Dahod, where he has a house on Dahod-Indore Highway and has been doing business of milk selling and keeping buffaloes and goats.

Opponent No.1 i.e. driver was driving the Tempo bearing registration No.MP-09-KA-9878 in rash and negligent manner and while negotiating turn, the said tempo came to the house of the applicant, wherein one buffalo, one calf and one goat died in the accident and one buffalo and one calf got seriously injured and ultimately, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1990/2012 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/09/2024 undefined
tempo dashed with the wall of the house of the applicant whereby the wall got damaged and also damaged the motorcycle lying in front of the house.
Therefore, the applicant has filed claim petition for damages claiming compensation of Rs.1.5 lakhs against the present respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponents No.1 & 2 have chosen not to appear and contest the claim petition.
Opponent No.3 - insurance company of the Tempo has appeared and filed its written statement / objections, by disputing all the averments made by the claimant in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.
2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal is preferred by the claimant for enhancement.

3. Learned advocate Mr. Saiyed for the appellant - original claimant has submitted that the Tribunal has granted very meager amount as against the damages.
He has submitted that the tempo is the sole negligent for the accident in question and therefore, the damages as claimed by the appellant may be granted.

He has submitted that the Tribunal has not properly evaluated all the evidence /
documentary as well as oral and granted compensation in very conservatively, which should be higher.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has exonerated the insurance company on the ground that the driver was not holding valid driving license.
In fact, the tempo in question is a light motor vehicle and the driver was holding driving license for light motor vehicle.
Therefore, all the opponents i.e. driver, owner and insurance company may be held liable jointly and severally.
He has submitted that this appeal may be allowed accordingly.

4. Per contra, learned advocate Mr. Mazmudar for the insurance company has submitted that the impugned judgment and award is just and proper and there is no infirmity or illegality committed by the Tribunal.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has rightly assessed the quantum and no interference be made by this Court.

He has submitted that the Tribunal has taken into consideration all NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1990/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined the evidence on record and passed the impugned judgment and award.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has rightly exonerated the insurance company as the driver of the tempo was not holding valid driving license.
He has submitted that this appeal may be dismissed.
5. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.
It also endeavors to make good the human suffering to the extent possible and to also save families which have lost their breadwinners from being pushed to wandering.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6. I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties.
I have perused the impugned judgment and award passed by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1990/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined learned Tribunal.
I have also considered the documents available on record.

From the record, it transpires that there is no dispute with regard to the fact that the tempo driver has lost control over the tempo and dashed with the buffaloes, goats, motorcycle lying in front of the house of the appellant and wall of the house of the appellant.
There is also no dispute that the tempo driver was not holding driving license.
The only dispute is that the tempo driver was not holding effective driving license.
The driver was holding driving license of LMV and the tempo was a goods vehicle and therefore, the Tribunal has considered that the HGV license is required to drive the tempo.
At this stage, it would be fruitful to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited versus Zaharulnisha reported in AIR 2008 SC 2218.

3 by the Hon'ble Apex Court, it would be proper to order pay and recover, which would meet the ends of justice.

7. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
7.1 The appeal is partly allowed, by holding that all NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1990/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined the opponents are liable to the compensation jointly and severally.

7.2 The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire awarded amount, if yet not deposited,
with interest and cost as decided by the Tribunal, from the date of claim petition till its realisation,
within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
It would be open for the insurance company to recover the said amount from the other tort-feasor/s in accordance with law.

7.3 The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal (including enhanced amount), with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
7.4 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
7.5 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
